description: Demo economic inputs for replacing exactly one carbide cutting insert. Public references, internal contract fixtures, and explicit synthetic policy assumptions are recorded separately; none of the values are an actual site quotation, payroll record, MES result, or guaranteed maintenance cost.

derivation.formula: round(139942 / (8 * 60)) = 292 KRW/min; round(292 * 1.5) = 438 KRW/min for the single night-work premium demo rate

limitations: The survey wage is a manufacturing cost reference, not this site's ordinary wage or payroll rate.
The 438 KRW/min value applies one 50% night-work premium only. Overtime/holiday overlap, benefits, and contractor overhead are not calculated.

execution_time_policy.reasoning: The Backend owns calculated_at. Immediate maintenance uses that instant and the demo planned window uses calculated_at + 12 hours as cost-calculation assumptions, not approved Work Order schedules. Both are converted to Asia/Seoul before the 22:00-06:00 night-work band is selected.
execution_time_policy.limitations: This is a deterministic demo policy, not a payroll engine. It does not infer overtime from a shift calendar or stack overtime, holiday, and night premiums.

labor_duration_minutes.reasoning: Sandvik training examples use one to two minutes for direct insert indexing, while a published human-centric SMED equipment-replacement example reports 9:10 after improvement and 13:04 before improvement when preparation, disassembly, assembly, adjustment, and control are included. Ten minutes is therefore used only as a demo end-to-end hands-on duration, with 5-15 minutes retained as sensitivity rather than claimed as a manufacturer standard.

external_service_cost_minor.reasoning: The representative GS-002 fixture records spare_part_available=true. This demo policy assumes an in-house insert replacement with no vendor dispatch; zero means the cost is structurally not incurred, not that an unknown vendor quote was replaced with zero.

expected_downtime_minutes.reasoning: The existing TOOL_REPLACEMENT What-if contract fixes preventive downtime at 30 minutes. The 15-45 minute band preserves that canonical demo midpoint and exposes uncertainty for safe stop, access, replacement, verification, test run, and restart. The 120-minute GS-002 event impact is not reused because it represents unplanned production exposure rather than planned insert-replacement downtime.

production_loss_rate_minor_per_minute.reasoning: The repository's synthetic capacity model uses OEE 0.846 and a four-minute demo cycle, producing 0.2115 effective units per minute. AI4I contains no selling price, manufacturing cost, contribution margin, MES takt, or ERP economics, so the 4,000/5,000/6,000 KRW per-unit contribution-margin band is an explicit demo assumption and must be replaced by site ERP data before real use.

derivation.formula: parts_cost + emergency_labor_duration * labor_rate + unplanned_downtime * production_loss_rate = 67391 / 147971 / 334331 KRW

failure_consequence_cost_minor.reasoning: The consequence band combines one replacement insert, reference maintenance labor, and unplanned production interruption. The 60/120/240-minute band is anchored to the repository's synthetic event-impact range, with GS-002 providing the 120-minute midpoint. Scrap, rework, restart consumables, secondary damage, and contractual penalties are excluded because no governed values exist.

expected_failure_loss_minor.reasoning: Expected failure loss is a calculated output, not a site master value. Only probabilities already present in the governed demo What-if contract are used. Cost What-if does not interpolate or create future Prediction values.
expected_failure_loss_minor.missing_probability_behavior: Return insufficient for that timing; do not estimate, interpolate, or substitute a probability.

sources.title: The Human-Centric SMED
sources.evidence: Table 2 reports equipment-replacement task totals of 13:04 as-is and 9:10 after improvement, including preparation, disassembly, assembly, adjustment, control, movement, and order.

sources.title: Design-for-Cost - An Approach for Distributed Manufacturing Cost Estimation
sources.evidence: NIST describes cost breakdown and the formulas machining cost = machine rate * time and labor cost = labor rate * labor operation time; it also notes that assumptions are required when source data are unavailable.

sources.title: World-Class OEE: Set Targets To Drive Improvement
sources.evidence: The common benchmark components 90% availability, 95% performance, and 99% quality multiply to approximately 85% OEE; the source also warns that there is no universal ideal target.

sources.title: AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance Dataset
sources.evidence: AI4I is a synthetic predictive-maintenance dataset with sensor, tool-wear, and failure variables; its documented variables do not include price, margin, takt, MES, or ERP economics.

sources.title: Production planning context v1
sources.evidence: The synthetic capacity model records OEE 0.846, a four-minute demo cycle, and 12.69 units/hour per asset.

sources.evidence: The representative event records spare_part_available=true and estimated unplanned downtime of 120 minutes.

sources.title: TOOL_REPLACEMENT What-if contract fixture
sources.evidence: The contract fixture records 30 minutes of preventive downtime, baseline probability 0.82, intervention probability 0.21, and synthetic counterfactual limitations.

usage_policy.allowed: Demo decision-support calculation and sensitivity analysis with exact source and assumption provenance.
usage_policy.forbidden: Representing synthetic policy values as an actual site quote, payroll, MES/ERP result, guaranteed saving, recommendation, approval, or execution command.
usage_policy.missing_future_probability_behavior: Return insufficient for planned_window and reinspect_after until an authoritative probability or an explicitly governed sensitivity input is provided.
usage_policy.replacement_policy: Replace public and synthetic references with versioned site quote, payroll, MES, ERP, and observed maintenance-history inputs before operational use.
